question: The band of seven colours obtained on a screen due to dispersion is called _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Spectrum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dispersion** occurs when a ray of white light passes through a prism, splitting into its constituent colors. This phenomenon is due to the variation in the refractive index of the material for different wavelengths of light.
 
• The band of seven colors produced on a screen as a result of dispersion is called a **spectrum**. These colors include **violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, and red (VIBGYOR)**.
 
• Each color in the spectrum corresponds to a specific wavelength of visible light, with **violet** having the shortest wavelength and **red** having the longest.
 
• The phenomenon of dispersion and the formation of a spectrum were scientifically explained by **Isaac Newton**, who demonstrated that white light is composed of multiple colors.
 
• This property of light is crucial in understanding optical phenomena, such as rainbows, which are natural examples of spectrum formation due to dispersion of light through water droplets in the atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Definition of Dispersion:** Dispersion refers to the splitting of white light into its constituent colors when it passes through a medium like a prism. It occurs because different colors of light travel at different speeds when passing through a medium.
 
• **Applications of Spectrum:**
 
 
• **Spectroscopy:** Used in scientific fields to analyze the composition of substances based on their light spectrum.
 
• **Optical Instruments:** Instruments like spectrometers and spectrophotometers rely on dispersion and spectrum analysis.
 
• **Astronomy:** Astronomers use spectra to study the composition and movement of celestial bodies.
 
 
 
• **Refractive Index:** The refractive index of a material determines the degree of bending of light and varies with the wavelength of light, leading to dispersion.
 
• **Real-World Examples:**
 
 
• **Rainbows:** Formed by the dispersion and total internal reflection of sunlight in water droplets.
 
• **CDs and DVDs:** The grooves on the surface act as a diffraction grating, creating a spectrum.
 
 
 
• **Other Phenomena Related to Light:**
 
 
• **Reflection:** Bouncing back of light when it hits a surface.
 
• **Refraction:** Bending of light as it passes from one medium to another.
 
• **Diffraction:** The bending of light around obstacles or openings.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Isaac Newton's Experiment:** Newton demonstrated dispersion using a glass prism and white light, proving that sunlight consists of different colors.
 
• **Color Wavelengths:** The visible spectrum ranges from approximately **400 nm (violet)** to **700 nm (red)**.
 
• **Prism Material:** The degree of dispersion depends on the material of the prism; for example, glass disperses light more than air.
 
• **Difference Between Spectrum and Image:** A spectrum is a band of colors due to dispersion, whereas an image is a reproduction of an object through reflection or refraction.
